Weighted Mean or Mode of Raster Values by Polygon

Source: R/extract_weighted_by_poly.R
extract_weighted_by_poly.Rd

Summarises each layer of a raster over each polygon, with every cell counting by the fraction of it inside the polygon times a weight: its area by default, or a count such as population.

Usage

extract_weighted_by_poly(
  raster,
  poly,
  stat = c("mean", "mode"),
  weights = NULL,
  iteration = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

Arguments

raster

A SpatRaster, one or more layers.

poly

A SpatVector or sf object of polygons, in the CRS of raster.

stat

"mean" (default) or "mode".

weights

NULL (default) for area weights, or a single-layer SpatRaster of weights.

iteration

Deprecated; use label.

id

Optional name of the column of poly identifying the polygons. When NULL, ID or ID_adm_div is used when present.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

Value

A c4e_tbl carrying the raster's context, with one row per polygon: the attributes of poly, then one column per layer of raster, named after it.

Details

Each cell counts by \(f_c w_c\), where \(f_c\) is the fraction of the cell inside the polygon (exactextractr::exact_extract()) and \(w_c\) the weight of the cell:

  • weights = NULL: the cell area in km2. On a lon-lat grid cells shrink towards the poles, so area weights differ from a plain average of cells.

  • weights a SpatRaster, e.g. population: the polygon value describes the conditions where people live rather than the territory. A weight raster on another grid is put on the grid of raster with align_count_rast(), so it must hold counts.

A polygon whose weights are all zero (no population) falls back to the coverage fractions alone. Cells where raster is NA are ignored; a polygon with no valid cell gets NA.

stat = "mean" returns the weighted mean, for continuous layers. stat = "mode" returns the class with the largest total weight, for class layers (land cover, climate zones); ties go to the lowest class.

See also

extract_by_poly() for unweighted statistics, align_count_rast(), exactextractr::exact_extract()

Examples

r <- terra::rast(xmin = 0, xmax = 2, ymin = 0, ymax = 1, res = 1,
                 crs = "epsg:4326", vals = c(10, 20))
names(r) <- "value"
pop <- terra::rast(r, vals = c(1, 3))
p <- terra::vect(terra::ext(0, 2, 0, 1), crs = "epsg:4326")
p$id <- 1

extract_weighted_by_poly(r, p)                 # area: about 15
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#> # Context:  summary
#>      id value
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1    15
extract_weighted_by_poly(r, p, weights = pop)  # people: 17.5
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#> # Context:  summary
#>      id value
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1  17.5
